Thanks for the context. High-level legal assessment and suggested compromise below. I copied Aaron Mills (Helios counsel) on a separate note to clarify a couple items — I'll summarize the requested clarifications to keep the thread readable for commercial.

Legal assessment (concise):
- Right-to-defend: we typically offer right-to-defend only for direct infringement claims stemming from our hosted model outputs when the customer provides prompt notice and preserves evidence. Allowing unconditional right-to-defend increases control and risk for Redwood (we may be contractually bound to litigation strategy that is suboptimal).
- OSS & training-data carveouts: reasonable to agree to carveouts, but we should define narrowly ("OSS as included under a maintained SPDX list and training-data-origin claims limited to provably licensed datasets").
- Evidence/notice timelines: 30 days notice is reasonable; technical evidence within 10 business days may be tight — propose 15 business days for complex replay and log export.
- Insurance/escrow: we can provide current insurance certificate; we cannot accept an escrow requirement without explicit limit and trigger (propose escrow threshold > $5M or only after insurance exhaustion).

Proposed commercial compromise for Helios:
- Mutual defense-promises: Redwood will accept right-to-defend for covered third-party IP claims limited to model-output infringement, subject to: (a) prompt notice, (b) Redwood control of defense with customer cooperation, (c) customer's ability to participate at its expense; (d) explicit OSS/training-data carveouts as discussed.
- If a customer insists on a defend-by-customer clause, offer a reimbursement path where Redwood pays defense costs up to a cap.
- Operational addendum documenting evidence collection process (who collects logs, retention windows, contact points).

Ask for commercial: Ben, if we offer right-to-defend under these limits, what concession (price/commitment) should we request? My read: a 12–18 month minimum usage commitment + a modest uplift or credit for shared defense costs.

Next steps:
- Ben: propose commercial terms (by EOD Wed)
- Logan: I will draft a short defense-control clause and narrow OSS/training-data language (ETA: Thu morning)
- Ben/Logan: sync with Helios procurement after we have legal language and commercial terms.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference

Logan / Kim / Ben — thanks for the fast turnaround and the proposed path. Helios reviewed your suggested carveouts and timeline adjustments with counsel (Aaron is copied). A quick recap and next asks: 

- Helios is generally comfortable with Redwood controlling defense for covered model-output infringement, provided Redwood commits to a documented evidence collection process and a single point of contact in Ops for forensics.
- Helios accepts the OSS carveout if Redwood provides the SPDX list and confirms no secret dependencies will be treated as Redwood-origin claims.
- We can accept a 15-business-day window for technical evidence, but Helios needs automated log exports retained for 90 days (our security and compliance requirement).
- For escrow: Helios will move from a standing escrow ask to a contingent escrow trigger (post-judgment > $5M). Helios requests an insurance certificate before countersignature and a standard Cycles-of-Review clause for any future material model changes that might affect exposure.

Attached is our updated insurance cert: Helios_Insurance_Certificate.pdf. If Redwood can send a short redline with the mutual defense language and the OSS definition by EOD Friday, procurement will route DocuSign next week.
